title: Lakers rookie Cameron Carr credits Baylor experience for growth
text:
Lakers rookie Cameron Carr credits Baylor experience for growth
Los Angeles Lakers rookie Cameron Carr is focusing on developing his skills and contributing to the team, according to an Aug. 11 report. Carr’s work ethic and willingness to improve have been highlighted since joining the franchise.
Carr’s approach was shaped during his time at Baylor University, where he sat out a season after transferring from Tennessee. Baylor coach Scott Drew said that period allowed Carr to learn from Philadelphia 76ers player VJ Edgecombe. “The smart take from the strong,” Drew said of Carr learning from Edgecombe. “You’re always going to see his work ethic, see how he did things, his approach. And Cam was able to learn from that, and take from that as well.”
Instead of disengaging while sidelined, Carr joined Baylor’s scout team and regularly competed against Edgecombe, who later became the third overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft. Drew said this experience helped mature Carr’s game: “He went from somebody at the beginning of the year that maybe people didn’t know about, to being at the front of the scouting report,” Drew said. “That’s something that he wasn’t on at Tennessee. The adjustment from a great summer and then great start to the year, to all of a sudden things became a lot harder for him from the standpoint – he was the most targeted man defensively.”
“(Opposing teams could say), ‘Don’t leave him alone, make sure you know where he is at all times, a lot of help in the gaps,’” Drew continued. “He was able to let his game mature from another standpoint of being the marked man out there.”
Carr now faces competition for playing time with Los Angeles but has shown readiness by embracing challenges in college and demonstrating commitment during practices. His athleticism has also been recognized; NBA 2K27 ranks him fourth in vertical leap among players.
